notes: Before anything starts, Nodeau can now show you where a model would run, what it would cost and why. Run nodeau run with --explain, or press Preview in app.nodeau.ai, and you get the machine and accelerator Nodeau would choose across your fleet, the memory the model is expected to need, what is available right now, how much Nodeau keeps back for your system and whether that figure was measured on your machine or is Nodeau's conservative default, and every other machine's reason. Every number says where it came from: measured, estimated, observed right now or Nodeau's own policy. The safety reserve now has two parts: a floor that is never given away, and a margin above it that you can set aside for one run on the one machine you were shown, with the new arithmetic in front of you before you agree. When the hardware itself is too small, no override is offered. New: nodeau benchmark measures how much memory this machine needs to keep for itself, and a Mac can measure a model's own footprint. Nothing changes until you adopt the result with nodeau benchmark adopt, and nodeau benchmark reset puts the conservative default back. A calibration lasts 30 days and is set aside by itself when the operating system, the hardware or the driver changes, and nodeau doctor tells you which reserve each machine is using. On Linux a card's figure is the whole card's, and Nodeau says so. This release also includes everything in v0.18.0-beta.5. Version v0.19.0-beta.8 is a maintenance release. Removing a machine from your fleet with nodeau fleet remove now also retires its record in your account, so app.nodeau.ai stops listing it. The machine is removed on your own machine at once; if Nodeau Cloud cannot be reached at that moment, the request is kept and sent automatically until Nodeau Cloud confirms it, and nodeau fleet status shows when it has. A record is retired by the machine's own identity, never by its name, so a machine that joins again under the same name is listed as itself, and the retired record's history is kept. nodeau fleet remove also retires the records your account still holds of machines that already left this fleet under the name you give it, after listing them. When no machine can take a model, nodeau run --explain now describes the machine a one-run override would admit, rather than one nothing can help, and a fleet running this release puts that machine first in app.nodeau.ai's Preview too. After you adopt another machine's benchmark, nodeau benchmark adopt now prints the reset for that machine. When you upgrade the machine that runs your fleet, the fleet gateway your Macs are reached through is restarted onto the version you installed if it was running. This release also includes everything in v0.19.0-beta.7. Version v0.19.0-beta.9 is a maintenance release. When nodeau update finds a newer release, the command it prints now installs it where your Nodeau is installed, with the same installer a first install uses, so nodeau and nodeau-fleet are replaced together. With --download it names the release it verified. If your shell would still find another copy of nodeau first, for example one an earlier nodeau update --download said to put in /usr/local/bin, nodeau update says so and prints the one command that replaces that copy with the one you installed. To update from v0.19.0-beta.8 or earlier, use the command you installed with, curl -fsSL https://get.nodeau.ai/install.sh | bash, rather than the line those versions print after nodeau update --download, which installs nodeau alone into /usr/local/bin. This release also includes everything in v0.19.0-beta.8. Version v0.19.0-beta.11 is a maintenance release. Every command Nodeau prints to install or repair Nodeau now installs where the nodeau your shell runs is installed, the way nodeau update already did: when nodeau fleet connect cannot find the fleet connector, when nodeau install on a Mac finds no model runtime, and when nodeau is run from a temporary folder, which is never where the command installs. If your shell would still find another copy of nodeau first, the same remedy says so and prints the one command that replaces that copy with the one you installed. After the command nodeau update prints to repair a split installation has worked, nodeau update no longer goes on reporting the installation as split. This release also includes everything in v0.19.0-beta.9.
